general.language: The language of the program. Version 1 is in English (UK) only.
general.default_start_screen: Which screen opens when the program starts: the case library, the case you worked on last, or the Academy.
general.open_last_case_automatically: Reopens your most recent unfinished attempt as soon as the program opens.
general.date_format: How dates are written across the program, such as 03/02/2026 or 2026-02-03.
general.time_format: Shows times on a 24 hour clock (18:42) or a 12 hour clock (6:42 pm).
general.time_shown_in_evidence: Whether evidence times appear as recorded by the device, corrected for a known clock offset, or both side by side.
general.week_starts_on: The first day of the week in calendars, rotas and the timeline's day view.
general.number_format: How large numbers and decimals are written, for example 1,234.56 or 1 234,56.
general.currency_display: Shows money with a symbol (£180.00) or a code (GBP 180.00).
general.confirm_before_closing: Asks before the program closes, so you do not lose your place by accident.
profile.chosen_name: The name you picked on first launch. It appears on your profile badge and report sign-off. It is for show only.
profile.avatar: The small picture on your profile badge. Academy ranks and badges unlock extra frames.
profile.badge_style: What the profile badge at the top shows: your name and avatar, just the name, or just the avatar.
profile.show_academy_rank_on_badge: Adds your Academy rank, such as Junior Analyst, under your name on the badge.
profile.name_on_report_sign_off: Puts your chosen name on the sign-off line of exported reports. It never changes the marks.
profile.reset_profile: Clears your chosen name so the name choice appears again. Saves, settings and Academy progress are kept.
appearance.theme: The colour scheme: Light, Dark, High contrast, or Match my computer to follow your system setting.
appearance.accent_colour: The colour of buttons, links and highlights.
appearance.text_size: Makes all text in the program smaller or larger.
appearance.font: The typeface. Dyslexia friendly uses a clearer, more spaced font. Monospace for data tables lines up columns of figures.
appearance.line_spacing: The space between lines of text. Relaxed can make long documents easier to read.
appearance.layout_density: How tightly lists, buttons and panels are packed. Compact shows more at once; Spacious is easier to click.
appearance.corner_style: Square or rounded corners on panels, cards and buttons.
appearance.icon_style: Outline or filled icons in menus and buttons.
appearance.panel_arrangement: Where the evidence list sits in the workspace: on the left, on the right, or with notes along the bottom.
appearance.remember_panel_sizes: Keeps panel widths as you left them the next time you open a case.
appearance.interface_zoom: Scales the whole interface, from 75% to 200%.
appearance.tooltips: Whether small explanations appear when you hover over buttons, and how quickly.
appearance.show_status_bar: Shows a thin bar at the bottom with save status, the stage and the number of items.
accessibility.reduce_motion: Shortens or removes animations, including Academy effects and screen transitions.
accessibility.reduce_transparency: Replaces see-through backgrounds with solid colours.
accessibility.high_contrast_evidence_vie: Uses stronger contrast inside documents, tables and emails, even when the rest of the theme is normal.
accessibility.colour_blind_safe_palette: Swaps colours that are hard to tell apart for a palette suited to your type of colour vision. Labels always show as text too.
accessibility.focus_outline_thickness: How thick the outline is around whatever the keyboard is focused on.
accessibility.large_click_targets: Makes buttons and list rows bigger and easier to hit.
accessibility.underline_links: Underlines every link, not only on hover.
accessibility.strengthen_graph_and_timel: Draws thicker lines and borders in the link chart, timeline and map.
accessibility.reading_ruler: Shows a soft band that follows your pointer, to help keep your place in long text.
accessibility.screen_reader_descriptions: Adds text descriptions of charts, graphs and the map for screen readers.
accessibility.announce_saves_and_stage_c: Tells screen readers when the case saves or a new stage opens.
accessibility.avoid_flashing_effects: Removes flashes and fast blinking anywhere in the program.
accessibility.show_shortcut_hints_on_but: Shows each button's keyboard shortcut on the button itself.
sound.master_volume: The overall volume of every sound the program makes.
sound.interface_sounds: Small clicks and tones when you use buttons and menus.
sound.stage_unlock_chime: Plays a chime when a new stage of a case opens.
sound.warning_sound: Plays a tone when a training mode warning appears.
sound.academy_reward_sounds: Plays sounds when you earn XP, ranks and badges in the Academy.
sound.mute_when_the_window_is_not_in_foc: Silences sounds while you are using another program.
sound.sound_pack: The style of sounds: Quiet, Classic or Minimal.
gameplay.mode: Training gives hints and warnings before mistakes. Assessment gives neither and is the fairer test. This affects the score.
gameplay.hints_available: How many hint levels you can ask for on each objective. Each hint costs a few marks. This affects the score.
gameplay.procedural_warnings: In training mode, warns you once before a procedural mistake such as opening material outside your scope. This affects the score.
gameplay.show_stage_objectives: Shows every objective, only the required ones, or keeps the list collapsed.
gameplay.show_stretch_objectives: Shows the optional stretch objectives that earn extra credit.
gameplay.case_clock: Shows time worked on the case, time left against the case estimate, or hides the clock.
gameplay.pause_the_clock_when_idle: Stops counting time when you have not touched the program for a while.
gameplay.highlight_new_evidence: Marks items that arrived in the latest stage so they stand out in the list.
gameplay.message_from_the_case_lead: Shows case lead messages as a pop-up, in the brief panel, or both.
gameplay.confirm_before_submitting_a_rep: Asks for confirmation before you submit, because submitting ends the attempt.
gameplay.show_running_findings_count: Shows how many findings you have recorded on the Findings tab.
gameplay.debrief_detail: Shows a short summary of your result, or the full debrief with every finding and event.
gameplay.spoiler_protection_in_the_debri: Reveals the answers one key finding at a time, or all at once.
gameplay.allow_retry_after_submission: Lets you start a new attempt at a case you have already submitted.
viewers.rows_per_page: How many rows a table shows before it splits into pages.
viewers.show_row_numbers: Shows a number at the start of every table row.
viewers.highlight_search_matches: Highlights search words inside documents and tables.
viewers.wrap_long_text: Wraps long lines onto the next line instead of scrolling sideways.
viewers.default_view_for_data_files: Opens data files such as CSV as a table or as raw text.
viewers.email_header_view: Shows the main email headers, every header, or both.
viewers.message_thread_style: Shows phone messages as chat bubbles or as a plain list.
viewers.image_viewer_zoom: How images open: fitted to the window, at actual size, or filling the space.
viewers.image_metadata_panel: Shows an image's metadata beside it all the time, or only when you ask.
viewers.hex_preview_for_files: Shows a byte-by-byte view of files, never, on request, or always.
viewers.open_items_in: Opens evidence in tabs, or in a split view so you can compare two items.
viewers.remember_scroll_position: Returns to where you were when you reopen an item.
viewers.show_clock_offset_warnings: Warns you when an item's clock is known to be fast, slow or in another time zone.
viewers.mark_examined_items: Shows items you have examined with a tick, a faded row, or both.
timeline.default_zoom: How far in the timeline starts: a day, an hour, a minute, or everything at once.
timeline.group_by: Groups timeline events by person or thing, by source, or by type of evidence.
timeline.show_source_icons: Shows a small icon for the kind of evidence behind each event.
timeline.highlight_conflicts: Highlights events from different sources that disagree about the time.
timeline.colour_by_confidence: Colours events by how confident you are in them.
timeline.show_gap_markers: Marks long gaps in the timeline where nothing is recorded.
timeline.sort_order: Lists events oldest first or newest first.
timeline.snap_to_grid: Rounds events you add by hand to the nearest 5 minutes, 15 minutes or hour.
timeline.export_image_size: The size of the picture made when you export the timeline as an image.
graph.layout: How the link chart arranges people and things: spread naturally, in a circle, as a hierarchy, or on a grid.
graph.node_size: The size of each person or thing on the link chart.
graph.labels: When names appear on the link chart: always, on hover, or only for selected items.
graph.edge_style: Draws links as straight lines or curves.
graph.dashed_lines_for_links_without_evi: Draws links with no cited evidence as dashed lines so they stand out.
graph.show_link_strength: Makes links thicker the more evidence supports them.
graph.suggested_links: Whether the chart hints at connections the evidence might support.
graph.cluster_colouring: Colours groups of closely linked items the same.
graph.physics: Lets the chart move and settle by itself. Turn off to keep items where you put them.
graph.simplify_the_view_above: Hides labels and detail when the chart has more than this many items.
graph.mini_map: Shows a small overview of the whole chart in a corner.
map.base_map: The background of the map: plain, with place labels, or with a grid.
map.distance_units: Shows distances in miles or kilometres.
map.show_camera_ranges: Draws the area each camera covers.
map.show_cell_coverage_circles: Draws the rough area a phone mast covers. A phone could be anywhere inside it.
map.time_slider_speed: How fast points move when you play the time slider.
map.trail_length: How much of a person's or thing's past movement stays on the map.
map.cluster_nearby_points: Groups points that are close together into one marker until you zoom in.
map.show_scale_bar: Shows a scale bar so you can judge distances.
statements.layout: Shows statements next to each other or one above another.
statements.compare_up_to: How many statements can be open side by side at once.
statements.highlight_colours: The colours for agreeing and conflicting claims. Colour blind safe uses blue and orange.
statements.show_claim_numbers: Shows each claim's number, such as ST-2.3, beside it.
statements.offer_to_send_times_and_place: Shows buttons to send a claim's time to the timeline or its place to the map.
statements.show_running_count_of_conflic: Shows how many conflicts you have marked so far.
search.search_mode: Simple search takes plain words. Advanced adds filters for type, date, source and status.
search.case_sensitive: Treats capital and small letters as different when searching.
search.match_whole_words: Only finds whole words, so 'van' does not match 'advance'.
search.include_metadata_in_search: Also searches item metadata such as authors, devices and headers.
search.fuzzy_matching: Finds near matches and small spelling mistakes.
search.search_history_length: How many recent searches are remembered. Choose 0 to keep none.
search.remember_filters_between_sessions: Keeps your evidence list filters the next time you open the case.
search.result_highlight_colour: The colour used to highlight search matches.
osint.mock_browser_start_page: What the simulated web browser shows when you open it.
osint.show_page_addresses: Shows each page's web address in the address bar.
osint.capture_reminder: Reminds you to capture a page properly before you rely on it.
osint.hash_captures_automatically: Every capture is hashed so it can be shown to be unchanged. This is always on.
osint.show_privacy_badge_on_profiles: Marks profiles as public or private so you know what your authority covers.
osint.warn_before_opening_a_private_prof: Asks before opening a profile that is private.
osint.clue_overlays_on_images: Lets you ask for highlights on parts of an image that might help locate it.
osint.archive_date_style: How dates on archived page copies are written.
integrity.action_logging: Every action you take is logged with the time. This is always on, because marking and the replay depend on it.
integrity.log_detail: How much detail the action log shows. Detailed includes every view and search.
integrity.hash_display: Shows hashes in full or shortened to the first characters.
integrity.verify_hash_when_opening_an_or: Checks an original item's hash each time you open it, only the first time, or never (training mode only).
integrity.warn_about_continuity_gaps: Warns if you examine an item before logging its receipt.
integrity.ask_for_a_reason_when_opening_: Asks why you need an original rather than a working copy, always or only in training mode.
integrity.show_custody_timeline_on_items: Shows each item's chain of custody as a timeline in the viewer.
report.template: The layout of your report: Standard, a Short form, or Detailed.
report.citation_style: Cites evidence inline, such as (EV-012), or as footnotes.
report.check_citations_automatically: Checks that every finding in the report cites evidence before you submit.
report.page_size: Paper size for PDF exports: A4 or Letter.
report.export_font: The typeface used in exported reports.
report.include_evidence_list_appendix: Adds a list of the evidence you relied on at the end of the report.
report.include_link_chart_image: Adds a picture of your link chart to the report.
report.include_timeline_image: Adds a picture of your timeline to the report.
report.default_export: Which format the Export button makes first: PDF or Markdown.
report.spell_check: Underlines spelling mistakes while you write the report.
report.show_word_count: Shows how many words each report section has.
report.draft_autosave_interval: How often your report draft saves while you type.
replay.replay_speed: How fast the investigation replay plays through your attempt.
replay.replay_detail: Shows only the key moments, or every action you took.
replay.show_mistakes_on_the_replay: Marks traps and procedural mistakes on the replay track.
replay.show_suggested_route: Shows the case author's suggested route beside yours once the debrief is done.
replay.start_replay_automatically: Starts playing the replay as soon as you open it.
replay.dashboard_range: How many recent attempts the skills dashboard uses.
replay.dashboard_chart_style: Shows your five skill areas as a radar chart or as bars.
replay.best_scores_count_assessment_mode: Only counts assessment attempts for best scores, so training hints do not inflate them.
replay.show_suggested_next_steps: Shows plain suggestions on what to practise next, with links to lessons.
replay.reset_progress_history: Clears the history behind the skills dashboard. Case saves are not touched.
notes.default_finding_type: The label a new finding starts with. Assumption is the safest default until you have evidence.
notes.show_grade_fields_on_findings: Shows the source and information grade fields on every finding, or only when evidence is linked.
notes.link_selected_evidence_to_new_find: Adds the item you are looking at as a citation when you start a new finding.
notes.note_font_size: The text size in the notes panel.
notes.markdown_preview_in_notes: Shows formatted text, such as bold and lists, in your notes.
notes.findings_board_layout: Shows findings as a list, as cards, or grouped by stage.
saves.autosave_interval: How often the case saves while you work.
saves.autosave_after_key_actions: Also saves straight after important actions such as a request or a finding.
saves.backup_copies_kept: How many older copies of each save are kept, in case you need to go back.
saves.backup_folder: Where backup copies are kept: the program's folder or a folder you choose.
saves.save_when_closing: Saves automatically when you close a case, or asks first.
saves.export_all_saves: Makes one file containing all your saves, to move to another computer.
saves.import_saves: Brings in saves exported from another computer.
saves.show_storage_used: Shows how much space your cases, saves and settings take up.
saves.clear_caches: Removes temporary files the program can rebuild. Saves are not touched.
saves.delete_all_data: Removes every case, save, setting and Academy record from this computer. Asks twice.
library.sort_by: The order cases appear in the library.
library.view: Shows cases as cards in a grid or as a list.
library.show_difficulty_badges: Shows each case's difficulty, such as Beginner or Hard.
library.show_time_estimates: Shows how long each case is expected to take.
library.show_completed_cases: Keeps cases you have submitted in the library list.
library.confirm_before_removing_a_case: Asks before a case and its saves are removed.
library.verify_case_packs: Checks every case pack's hashes each time it opens, or only when the files have changed.
academy.academy_reminders: Offers the matching lesson the first time you open a tool you have not learned yet.
academy.tips_frequency: How often short tips appear while you work.
academy.contextual_help_icons: Shows small ? icons next to features that open the matching help article.
academy.what_is_this_mode: Allows the 'What is this?' mode, where you click any part of the screen for a short explanation.
academy.open_help_in: Opens the help centre in a side panel or in its own full window.
academy.help_search_history: How many recent help searches are remembered on this computer. Choose 0 to keep none.
academy.show_academy_rewards_on_profile: Shows avatar frames and badge borders you have unlocked in the Academy.
academy.reset_academy_progress: Clears your Academy XP, ranks and badges. Case saves are not touched.
shortcuts.shortcut_preset: A ready-made set of keyboard shortcuts: Default, Compact, or Mouse free for working without a mouse.
shortcuts.rebind_actions: Change the key for any of about 40 actions.
shortcuts.show_shortcut_sheet: Shows every shortcut on one sheet you can print.
shortcuts.reset_all_shortcuts: Puts every shortcut back to the default.
notifications.stage_unlock_banner: Shows a banner when a new stage opens.
notifications.autosave_notice: How saving is shown: a small icon, a pop-up, or not at all.
notifications.hint_available_indicator: Shows a small marker on objectives where a hint is available.
notifications.procedural_warning_style: Shows training warnings as a dialog that must be answered or as a banner.
notifications.notification_duration: How long pop-up notices stay on screen.
privacy.content_notice_at_case_start: Shows a short note about the case's themes before you start.
privacy.sensitive_content_warnings: Shows a warning before items marked as sensitive.
privacy.blur_images_until_opened: Blurs images in previews until you choose to open them.
privacy.hide_graphic_details: Hides graphic descriptions where a case offers a gentler version.
privacy.usage_data_collection: Investafiction never sends anything off your computer. This cannot be changed because there is nothing to send.
privacy.warn_before_opening_packs_from_o: Asks before importing a case pack that was not made by the starter pack authors.
advanced.case_author_mode: For case authors: loads unpacked case folders and shows extra checks while you build a case.
advanced.show_internal_ids_on_items: Shows internal ids such as ENT-P1 next to names.
advanced.developer_tools: Enables the browser developer tools inside the program window.
advanced.log_level: How much the program writes to its own technical log.
advanced.experimental_features: Turns on features that are still being tested and may change.
advanced.open_data_folder: Shows where your cases, saves and settings are kept on this computer.
advanced.export_diagnostics: Makes a local file with technical details for a bug report. It contains no case answers or personal data.
advanced.reset_all_settings: Puts every setting back to its default. Saves and Academy progress are not touched.
